e-620.knowledge_point: Finding the Acceleration Vector of a Particle Given Its Velocity Vector
e-620.problem:
The velocity vector $\mathbf{v} = \langle u, v \rangle$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
\mathbf{v} = \langle 12t+t^2, t^3+1\rangle.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $\mathbf{a}$.
e-620.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(12t+{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}+1)⟩ \\  & =⟨12+2t,\,3{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

e-7224.knowledge_point: Computing the Acceleration of a Particle at a Given Moment Given Its Velocity Vector
e-7224.problem:
The velocity vector $\mathbf{v} = \langle u, v \rangle,$ measured in $\textrm{m}/\textrm s,$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ seconds, is given by

$$
\mathbf{v} = \langle t^4-t^2, 2t^3\rangle.
$$

Find the acceleration vector and the magnitude of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=1.$
e-7224.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{4}-{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨4{t}^{3}-2t,\,6{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration at time $t=1,$ we substitute $t=1$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(1) & =⟨4(1)^{3}-2(1),6(1)^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨2,6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute $|\mathbf a(1)|\mathbin{:}$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}|a(1)| & =|⟨2,6⟩| \\  & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{6}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{40} \\  & =2\sqrt{10}\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

e-621.knowledge_point: Finding the Acceleration Vector of a Particle Given Its Position Vector
e-621.problem:
The position vector $\mathbf{r}$ of a particle $P$ (relative to a fixed origin $O$) at time $t$ is given by

$$
\mathbf{r} = \langle 4t^2+1, 3t^2-t\rangle.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $\mathbf{a}$.
e-621.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector. We can do this by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{t}^{2}+1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}-t)⟩ \\  & =⟨8t,\,6t-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(8t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6t-1)⟩ \\  & =⟨8,6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

e-7225.knowledge_point: Computing the Acceleration of a Particle at a Given Moment Given Its Position Vector
e-7225.problem:
The position vector $\mathbf{r},$ in meters, of a particle $P$ relative to a fixed origin $O$ at time $t$ seconds is given by

$$
\mathbf{r} = \left\langle t^{5}-t^2,\, t^2+6t-3 \right\rangle.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector and the magnitude of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=0.$
e-7225.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do this by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{5}-{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}+6t-3)⟩ \\  & =⟨5{t}^{4}-2t,\,2t+6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5{t}^{4}-2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t+6)⟩ \\  & =⟨20{t}^{3}-2,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration at time $t=0,$ we substitute $t=0$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(0) & =⟨20(0)^{3}-2,\,2⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute $|\mathbf a(0)|\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}|a(0)| & =|⟨-2,\,2⟩| \\  & =\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{8} \\  & =2\sqrt{2}\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Acceleration is the derivative of velocity componentwise. The chain rule gives d(e^{3t})/dt = 3e^{3t}, and the power rule gives d(t^3)/dt = 3t^2.

before.html:
Question 2
?

The velocity vector v=⟨u,v⟩ of a particle P at time t is given by v=⟨ln⁡(3t+2),sin⁡(2t+5)⟩,t>0. Calculate the acceleration vector a.

a
a=⟨33t+2,−cos⁡(2t+5)⟩
b
a=⟨13t+2,2cos⁡(2t+5)⟩
c
a=⟨33t+2,−2cos⁡(2t+5)⟩
d
a=⟨33t+2,2cos⁡(2t+5)⟩
e
a=⟨13t+2,cos⁡(2t+5)⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: Differentiate each velocity component using the chain rule: d ln(3t+2)/dt = 3/(3t+2) and d sin(2t+5)/dt = 2 cos(2t+5). Thus option d is correct.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
v=⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡(3t+2),\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t+5)⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a.$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3t+2)),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t+5))⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{3}{3t+2},2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+5)⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

The velocity vector v=⟨u,v⟩ of a particle P at time t is given by v=⟨ln⁡(3t+2),sin⁡(2t+5)⟩,t>0. Calculate the acceleration vector a.

a
a=⟨33t+2,−cos⁡(2t+5)⟩
b
a=⟨13t+2,2cos⁡(2t+5)⟩
c
a=⟨33t+2,−2cos⁡(2t+5)⟩
d
a=⟨33t+2,2cos⁡(2t+5)⟩
e
a=⟨13t+2,cos⁡(2t+5)⟩
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector: a=dvdt=⟨dudt,dvdt⟩=⟨ddt(ln⁡(3t+2)),ddt(sin⁡(2t+5))⟩=⟨33t+2,2cos⁡(2t+5)⟩

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms option d. Differentiating componentwise gives 3/(3t+2) and 2 cos(2t+5) by the chain rule. The deliberately submitted option a has an incorrect second component.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Acceleration Vector of a Particle Given Its Velocity Vector
content.problem:
The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
v=⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡(3t+2),\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t+5)⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a.$
content.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3t+2)),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t+5))⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{3}{3t+2},2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+5)⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3

The velocity vector v=⟨u,v⟩ of a particle P at time t is given by v=⟨3t,55t⟩. Calculate the acceleration vector a.

a
a=⟨3ln⁡|t|,55t⟩
b
a=⟨−3t2,55t+1ln⁡5⟩
c
a=⟨−3t2,55t⟩
d
a=⟨3ln⁡|t|,55t+1ln⁡5⟩
e
a=⟨−3t2,55tln⁡5⟩
Submit
Correct

To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector: a=dvdt=⟨dudt,dvdt⟩=⟨ddt(3t),ddt(55t)⟩=⟨3(−1t2),55t⋅5ln⁡5⟩=⟨−3t2,55t+1ln⁡5⟩

$$

before.html:
Question 4
?

The velocity vector v=⟨u,v⟩ of a particle P at time t is given by v=⟨t2,e2t⟩. Calculate the acceleration vector a.

a
a=⟨t,e2t⟩
b
 a=⟨2t,e2t⟩
c
a=⟨t2,e2t2⟩
d
a=⟨2t,2e2t⟩
e
a=⟨t2,e2t4⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: Acceleration is the componentwise derivative of velocity. Since d(t²)/dt = 2t and d(e^{2t})/dt = 2e^{2t}, option d is correct.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
v=⟨{t}^{2},\,{e}^{2t}⟩.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a.$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{2t})⟩ \\  & =⟨2t,\,2{e}^{2t}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

The velocity vector v=⟨u,v⟩ of a particle P at time t is given by v=⟨t2,e2t⟩. Calculate the acceleration vector a.

a
a=⟨t,e2t⟩
b
 a=⟨2t,e2t⟩
c
a=⟨t2,e2t2⟩
d
a=⟨2t,2e2t⟩
e
a=⟨t2,e2t4⟩
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

a=dvdt=⟨dudt,dvdt⟩=⟨ddt(t2),ddt(e2t)⟩=⟨2t,2e2t⟩

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms that acceleration is ⟨2t, 2e^{2t}⟩: differentiate t² using the power rule and e^{2t} using the chain rule. This matches option d; the deliberately submitted option c is incorrect.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Acceleration Vector of a Particle Given Its Velocity Vector
content.problem:
The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
v=⟨{t}^{2},\,{e}^{2t}⟩.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a.$
content.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{2t})⟩ \\  & =⟨2t,\,2{e}^{2t}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

$$
v=⟨3{t}^{3},\,-\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2}⟩.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a$ at time $t=3.$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨9{t}^{2},\,-t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the acceleration at time $t=3,$ we substitute $t=3$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(3) & =⟨9(3)^{2},\,-3⟩ \\  & =⟨9\cdot 9,\,-3⟩ \\  & =⟨81,\,-3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Question 6
?

The velocity vector v=⟨u,v⟩ of a particle P at time t is given by v=⟨3t3,−12t2⟩. Calculate the acceleration vector a at time t=3.

a
a(3)=⟨81,3⟩
b
a(3)=⟨81,−3⟩
c
a(3)=⟨27,3⟩
d
a(3)=⟨9,−3⟩
e
a(3)=⟨27,−3⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

a=dvdt=⟨dudt,dvdt⟩=⟨ddt(3t3),ddt(−12t2)⟩=⟨9t2,−t⟩

Finally, to find the acceleration at time t=3, we substitute t=3 into the above:

a(3)=⟨9(3)2,−3⟩=⟨9⋅9,−3⟩=⟨81,−3⟩

after.name: Question 7
after.problem:
The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩,$ measured in $\text{m}/\text{s},$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ seconds, is given by

$$
v=⟨6t+1,-3{t}^{2}⟩.
$$

Find the magnitude of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=1.$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6t+1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-3{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨6,\,-6t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration at time $t=1,$ we substitute $t=1$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(1) & =⟨6,-6(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨-6,6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute $|a(1)|:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}|a(1)| & =|⟨-6,6⟩| \\  & =\sqrt{(-6)^{2}+({6}^{2})} \\  & =\sqrt{2\cdot 36} \\  & =6\sqrt{2}\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 7
?

The velocity vector v=⟨u,v⟩, measured in m/s, of a particle P at time t seconds, is given by v=⟨6t+1,−3t2⟩. Find the magnitude of the acceleration of P at time t=1.

a
6m/s2
b
52m/s2
c
0m/s2
d
62m/s2
e
35m/s2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

a=dvdt=⟨dudt,dvdt⟩=⟨ddt(6t+1),ddt(−3t2)⟩=⟨6,−6t⟩

To find the acceleration at time t=1, we substitute t=1 into the above: a(1)=⟨6,−6(1)⟩=⟨−6,6⟩

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute |a(1)|:

|a(1)|=|⟨−6,6⟩|=(−6)2+(62)=2⋅36=62m/s2.

verification.explanation: Differentiating gives a(t) = ⟨6, -6t⟩, so a(1) = ⟨6, -6⟩ and its magnitude is √72 = 6√2 m/s². The worked solution swaps the components in one line, but this leaves the magnitude unchanged and confirms option d.

content.knowledge_point: Computing the Acceleration of a Particle at a Given Moment Given Its Velocity Vector
content.problem:
The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩,$ measured in $\text{m}/\text{s},$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ seconds, is given by

$$
v=⟨6t+1,-3{t}^{2}⟩.
$$

Find the magnitude of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=1.$
content.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6t+1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-3{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨6,\,-6t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration at time $t=1,$ we substitute $t=1$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(1) & =⟨6,-6(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨-6,6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute $|a(1)|:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}|a(1)| & =|⟨-6,6⟩| \\  & =\sqrt{(-6)^{2}+({6}^{2})} \\  & =\sqrt{2\cdot 36} \\  & =6\sqrt{2}\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 8

The velocity vector v=⟨u,v⟩ of a particle P at time t is given by v=⟨ln⁡(3t+1),1−t2⟩,t>0. Calculate the acceleration vector a at time t=2.

a
a(2)=⟨35,−7⟩
b
a(2)=⟨ln⁡3,−7⟩
c
a(2)=⟨ln⁡7,−4⟩
d
a(2)=⟨37,−2⟩
e
a(2)=⟨37,−4⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: Differentiate velocity componentwise: a(t) = ⟨3/(3t+1), -2t⟩. Substituting t = 2 gives ⟨3/7, -4⟩, matching option e.

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
v=⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡(3t+1),1-{t}^{2}⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a$ at time $t=2.$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3t+1)),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{3}{3t+1},-2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the acceleration at time $t=2,$ we substitute $t=2$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(2) & =⟨\frac{3}{3(2)+1},-2(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{3}{7},-4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Question 8

The velocity vector v=⟨u,v⟩ of a particle P at time t is given by v=⟨ln⁡(3t+1),1−t2⟩,t>0. Calculate the acceleration vector a at time t=2.

a
a(2)=⟨35,−7⟩
b
a(2)=⟨ln⁡3,−7⟩
c
a(2)=⟨ln⁡7,−4⟩
d
a(2)=⟨37,−2⟩
e
a(2)=⟨37,−4⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector: a=dvdt=⟨dudt,dvdt⟩=⟨ddt(ln⁡(3t+1)),ddt(1−t2)⟩=⟨33t+1,−2t⟩

Finally, to find the acceleration at time t=2, we substitute t=2 into the above: a(2)=⟨33(2)+1,−2(2)⟩=⟨37,−4⟩

content.knowledge_point: Computing the Acceleration of a Particle at a Given Moment Given Its Velocity Vector
content.problem:
The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
v=⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡(3t+1),1-{t}^{2}⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a$ at time $t=2.$
content.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3t+1)),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{3}{3t+1},-2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

after.worked_solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{2}-4t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5t-{t}^{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨4t-4,\,5-3{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}

$$

The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
v=⟨2{t}^{2}-4t,5t-{t}^{3}⟩.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a$ at time $t=2.$
content.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{2}-4t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5t-{t}^{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨4t-4,\,5-3{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the acceleration at time $t=2,$ we substitute $t=2$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(2) & =⟨4(2)-4,\,5-3(2)^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨8-4,\,5-12⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,-7⟩\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 10
after.problem:
The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩,$ measured in $\text{m}/\text{s},$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ seconds is given by

$$
v=⟨{t}^{2}+2t,6{t}^{2}-3⟩.
$$

Find the magnitude of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=0.$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}+2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6{t}^{2}-3)⟩ \\  & =⟨2t+2,\,12t⟩\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}a(0) & =⟨2(0)+2,12(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨2,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}|a(0)| & =|⟨2,0⟩| \\  & =\sqrt{(2)^{2}+(0)} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.\end{aligned}

The position vector r(t) of a particle P relative to a fixed origin O at time t is given by r(t)=⟨3t3+t,ln⁡t⟩,t>0. Calculate the acceleration vector a.

a
 a=⟨9t2+1,1t⟩
b
a=⟨18t,−1t2⟩

a=⟨18,1t2⟩
d

decision.explanation: Acceleration is the second derivative of position. The first derivative is ⟨9t²+1, 1/t⟩, and the second is ⟨18t, −1/t²⟩, matching option b.

after.name: Question 12
after.problem:
The position vector $r(t)$ of a particle $P$ relative to a fixed origin $O$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
r(t)=⟨3{t}^{3}+t,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡t⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a.$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do this by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{3}+t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨9{t}^{2}+1,\,\frac{1}{t}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(9{t}^{2}+1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t})⟩ \\  & =⟨18t,\,-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

after.html:
Question 12
?

The position vector r(t) of a particle P relative to a fixed origin O at time t is given by r(t)=⟨3t3+t,ln⁡t⟩,t>0. Calculate the acceleration vector a.

a
 a=⟨9t2+1,1t⟩
b
a=⟨18t,−1t2⟩
c
a=⟨18,1t2⟩
d
 a=⟨18t,−2t⟩
e
 a=⟨9t2+1,−1t2⟩
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do this by differentiating the position vector:

v=drdt=⟨dxdt,dydt⟩=⟨ddt(3t3+t),ddt(ln⁡t)⟩=⟨9t2+1,1t⟩

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

a=dvdt=⟨dudt,dvdt⟩=⟨ddt(9t2+1),ddt(1t)⟩=⟨18t,−1t2⟩

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms that differentiating position twice gives a = ⟨18t, −1/t²⟩, matching option b. Option e incorrectly retains the first velocity component.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Acceleration Vector of a Particle Given Its Position Vector
content.problem:
The position vector $r(t)$ of a particle $P$ relative to a fixed origin $O$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
r(t)=⟨3{t}^{3}+t,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡t⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a.$
content.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do this by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{3}+t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨9{t}^{2}+1,\,\frac{1}{t}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(9{t}^{2}+1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t})⟩ \\  & =⟨18t,\,-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Question 13
?

The position vector r of a particle P (relative to a fixed origin O) at time t is given by r=⟨4t3−21,2t4+3t⟩. Calculate the acceleration vector a.

a
a=⟨8t,12t2⟩
b
a=⟨24t,24t2⟩
c
a=⟨12t,8t2+3⟩
d
a=⟨12t2,8t3+3⟩
e
a=⟨24t,12t2⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: Differentiate position twice. Velocity is ⟨12t², 8t³+3⟩, so acceleration is ⟨24t, 24t²⟩, matching option b.

after.name: Question 13
after.problem:
The position vector $r$ of a particle $P$ (relative to a fixed origin $O$) at time $t$ is given by

$$
r=⟨4{t}^{3}-21,2{t}^{4}+3t⟩.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a.$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do this by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{t}^{3}-21),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{4}+3t)⟩ \\  & =⟨12{t}^{2},\,8{t}^{3}+3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(12{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(8{t}^{3}+3)⟩ \\  & =⟨24t,\,24{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 16
after.problem:
The position vector $r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ relative to a fixed origin $O$ at time $t$ seconds is given by

$$
r=⟨4{t}^{3/2}+4{t}^{2}+5,\,{t}^{3}-4{t}^{2}+t⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the magnitude of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=1.$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do this by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{t}^{3/2}+4{t}^{2}+5),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}-4{t}^{2}+t)⟩ \\  & =⟨6{t}^{1/2}+8t,\,3{t}^{2}-8t+1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6{t}^{1/2}+8t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}-8t+1)⟩ \\  & =⟨3{t}^{-1/2}+8,\,6t-8⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration at time $t=1,$ we substitute $t=1$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(1) & =⟨3(1)^{-1/2}+8,\,6(1)-8⟩ \\  & =⟨3+8,\,6-8⟩ \\  & =⟨11,\,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute $|a(1)|:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|a(1)| & =|⟨11,\,-2⟩| \\  & =\sqrt{{11}^{2}+(-2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{125} \\  & =5\sqrt{5}\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}\end{aligned}

Question 16
?

The position vector r, in meters, of a particle P relative to a fixed origin O at time t seconds is given by r=⟨4t3/2+4t2+5,t3−4t2+t⟩,t>0. Calculate the magnitude of the acceleration of P at time t=1.

a
55m/s2
b
53m/s2
c
23m/s2
d
35m/s2
e
5m/s2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do this by differentiating the position vector:

v=drdt=⟨dxdt,dydt⟩=⟨ddt(4t3/2+4t2+5),ddt(t3−4t2+t)⟩=⟨6t1/2+8t,3t2−8t+1⟩

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

a=dvdt=⟨dudt,dvdt⟩=⟨ddt(6t1/2+8t),ddt(3t2−8t+1)⟩=⟨3t−1/2+8,6t−8⟩

To find the acceleration at time t=1, we substitute t=1 into the above:

a(1)=⟨3(1)−1/2+8,6(1)−8⟩=⟨3+8,6−8⟩=⟨11,−2⟩

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute |a(1)|:

|a(1)|=|⟨11,−2⟩|=112+(−2)2=125=55m/s2

content.knowledge_point: Computing the Acceleration of a Particle at a Given Moment Given Its Position Vector
content.problem:
The position vector $r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ relative to a fixed origin $O$ at time $t$ seconds is given by

$$
r=⟨4{t}^{3/2}+4{t}^{2}+5,\,{t}^{3}-4{t}^{2}+t⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the magnitude of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=1.$
content.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do this by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{t}^{3/2}+4{t}^{2}+5),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}-4{t}^{2}+t)⟩ \\  & =⟨6{t}^{1/2}+8t,\,3{t}^{2}-8t+1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6{t}^{1/2}+8t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}-8t+1)⟩ \\  & =⟨3{t}^{-1/2}+8,\,6t-8⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration at time $t=1,$ we substitute $t=1$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(1) & =⟨3(1)^{-1/2}+8,\,6(1)-8⟩ \\  & =⟨3+8,\,6-8⟩ \\  & =⟨11,\,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute $|a(1)|:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|a(1)| & =|⟨11,\,-2⟩| \\  & =\sqrt{{11}^{2}+(-2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{125} \\  & =5\sqrt{5}\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 17
?

The position vector r of a particle P (relative to a fixed origin O) at time t is given by r=⟨ln⁡(t+1),2t4+3⟩,t>0. Calculate the acceleration vector a at time t=1.

a
a(1)=⟨12,12⟩
b
a(1)=⟨−14,12⟩
c
a(1)=⟨12,16⟩
d
a(1)=⟨−12,24⟩
e
a(1)=⟨−14,24⟩
Submit

decision.explanation: Acceleration is the second derivative of position: a(t) = ⟨−1/(t+1)², 24t²⟩. At t = 1, this gives ⟨−1/4, 24⟩, matching option e.

after.name: Question 17
after.problem:
The position vector $r$ of a particle $P$ (relative to a fixed origin $O$) at time $t$ is given by

$$
r=⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+1),2{t}^{4}+3⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a$ at time $t=1.$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do this by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+1)),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{4}+3)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{t+1},8{t}^{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t+1}),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(8{t}^{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{(t+1)^{2}},24{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the acceleration at time $t=1,$ we substitute $t=1$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(1) & =⟨-\frac{1}{(1+1)^{2}},24({1}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{4},24⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Question 17
?

The position vector r of a particle P (relative to a fixed origin O) at time t is given by r=⟨ln⁡(t+1),2t4+3⟩,t>0. Calculate the acceleration vector a at time t=1.

a
a(1)=⟨12,12⟩
b
a(1)=⟨−14,12⟩
c
a(1)=⟨12,16⟩
d
a(1)=⟨−12,24⟩
e
a(1)=⟨−14,24⟩
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do this by differentiating the position vector: v=drdt=⟨dxdt,dydt⟩=⟨ddt(ln⁡(t+1)),ddt(2t4+3)⟩=⟨1t+1,8t3⟩

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector: a=dvdt=⟨dudt,dvdt⟩=⟨ddt(1t+1),ddt(8t3)⟩=⟨−1(t+1)2,24t2⟩

Finally, to find the acceleration at time t=1, we substitute t=1 into the above: a(1)=⟨−1(1+1)2,24(12)⟩=⟨−14,24⟩

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms a(t) = ⟨−1/(t+1)², 24t²⟩. At t = 1, a(1) = ⟨−1/4, 24⟩, matching option e. The deliberately submitted option b has an incorrect second component.

content.knowledge_point: Computing the Acceleration of a Particle at a Given Moment Given Its Position Vector
content.problem:
The position vector $r$ of a particle $P$ (relative to a fixed origin $O$) at time $t$ is given by

$$
r=⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+1),2{t}^{4}+3⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a$ at time $t=1.$
content.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do this by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+1)),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{4}+3)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{t+1},8{t}^{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t+1}),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(8{t}^{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{(t+1)^{2}},24{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the acceleration at time $t=1,$ we substitute $t=1$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(1) & =⟨-\frac{1}{(1+1)^{2}},24({1}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{4},24⟩\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5{t}^{3}-2{t}^{2}+3),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{4}-3{t}^{2}+1)⟩ \\  & =⟨15{t}^{2}-4t,\,4{t}^{3}-6t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(15{t}^{2}-4t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{t}^{3}-6t)⟩ \\  & =⟨30t-4,\,12{t}^{2}-6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration at time $t=2,$ we substitute $t=2$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(2) & =⟨30(2)-4,\,12(2)^{2}-6⟩ \\  & =⟨60-4,\,48-6⟩ \\  & =⟨56,\,42⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute $|a(2)|:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|a(2)| & =|⟨56,\,42⟩| \\  & =\sqrt{{56}^{2}+{42}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{3136+1764} \\  & =\sqrt{4900} \\  & =70\end{aligned}
$$

So, the magnitude of the acceleration at time $t=2\,\text{s}$ is $70{\text{ m/s}}^{2}.$

So, the magnitude of the acceleration at time t=2s is 70 m/s2.

decision.explanation: Differentiating position twice gives a(t) = ⟨8/(1+t)³, 2t⟩. At t = 1, a(1) = ⟨1, 2⟩, whose magnitude is √(1²+2²) = √5 m/s², matching option a.

after.name: Question 19
after.problem:
The position vector $r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ relative to a fixed origin $O$ at time $t$ seconds is given by

$$
r=⟨\frac{4}{1+t},\,\frac{{t}^{3}}{3}-4t+5⟩.
$$

Calculate the magnitude of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=1.$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do this by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{4}{1+t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{t}^{3}}{3}-4t+5)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{4}{(1+t)^{2}},\,{t}^{2}-4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\frac{4}{(1+t)^{2}}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-4)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{8}{(1+t)^{3}},\,2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration at time $t=1,$ we substitute $t=1$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(1) & =⟨\frac{8}{(1+(1))^{3}},\,2(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{8}{{2}^{3}},\,2⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute $|a(1)|:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|a(1)| & =|⟨1,\,2⟩| \\  & =\sqrt{(1)^{2}+(2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{5}\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

b

c
2m/s2

EXPLANATION

To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do this by differentiating the position vector:

v=drdt=⟨dxdt,dydt⟩=⟨ddt(41+t),ddt(t33−4t+5)⟩=⟨−4(1+t)2,t2−4⟩

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

a=dvdt=⟨dudt,dvdt⟩=⟨ddt(−4(1+t)2),ddt(t2−4)⟩=⟨8(1+t)3,2t⟩

To find the acceleration at time t=1, we substitute t=1 into the above:

a(1)=⟨8(1+(1))3,2(1)⟩=⟨823,2⟩=⟨1,2⟩

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute |a(1)|:

|a(1)|=|⟨1,2⟩|=(1)2+(2)2=5m/s2

after.name: Question 20
after.problem:
The position vector $r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ relative to a fixed origin $O$ at time $t$ seconds is given by

$$
r=⟨2{t}^{3}+3{t}^{2}+5t,\,2{t}^{4}-4{t}^{2}+t+1⟩.
$$

Calculate the magnitude of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=0.$
after.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do this by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3}+3{t}^{2}+5t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{4}-4{t}^{2}+t+1)⟩ \\  & =⟨6{t}^{2}+6t+5,\,8{t}^{3}-8t+1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6{t}^{2}+6t+5),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(8{t}^{3}-8t+1)⟩ \\  & =⟨12t+6,\,24{t}^{2}-8⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration at time $t=0,$ we substitute $t=0$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(0) & =⟨12(0)+6,\,24(0)-8⟩ \\  & =⟨6,\,-8⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute $|a(0)|:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|a(0)| & =|⟨6,\,-8⟩| \\  & =\sqrt{{6}^{2}+(-8)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{100} \\  & =10\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

a=dvdt=⟨dudt,dvdt⟩=⟨ddt(6t2+6t+5),ddt(8t3−8t+1)⟩=⟨12t+6,24t2−8⟩

To find the acceleration at time t=0, we substitute t=0 into the above:

a(0)=⟨12(0)+6,24(0)−8⟩=⟨6,−8⟩

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute |a(0)|:

|a(0)|=|⟨6,−8⟩|=62+(−8)2=100=10m/s2
